newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy new car registrations seen up again in July.
newsitem.headline: Italy new car registrations seen up again in July.

text.p: Italian new car registrations are expected to continue rising in July with a forecast jump of some 50 percent year-on-year to around 240,000 units, auto sector sources and analysts said.
In July 1996, new car registrations totalled 160,007.
Italy's Transport Ministry is due to issue the July 1997 data early next week.
In June, registrations surged 50.71 percent to 222,800 taking cumulative first half 1997 registrations to 1,312,400, a rise of 31.32 percent on the first six months of 1996.
Analysts said the market continued to be boosted by the government's incentive scheme to trade in old cars for new.
"If the market continues the same trend of recent months then we could even see July registrations of 250,000 to 260,000," said Gian Paolo Trasi of IMI-Sigeco brokers.

"There are two factors indicating a strong increase -- purchases made ahead of the originally planned end of the scheme in September, although it has now been extended, and the summer holidays," Trasi added.
